relevance_note: Case report of a girl with Blau syndrome/EOS carrying a heterozygous NOD2 variant shared with her asymptomatic father: "A novel C483W NOD2 mutation was identify in the proband and her asymptomatic father."
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; built the JSON with a short Python script in scratch, values typed from reading. In scope: the proband (label 'patient', single patient of the case report), her carrier father (asymptomatic), her mother (tested; variant not found, so no variant row), and the 'BS patient with documented R334W mutation' used as a positive control in the flow cytometry assay ('unnamed person 1'; described only with variant, diagnosis and assay results; included because the scope covers every person described with a NOD2 variant). Healthy controls (n = 3) have no NOD2 variant and are out of scope. Ages: onset recorded as the earliest symptom (rash 'suspect of atopic dermatitis' since 6 months); joint lumps since age 3 recorded as feature onset; last evaluation = age 9 at referral. Father's variant fields come from the Fig. 3 legend naming 'the patient and her father'; transcript and protein printed only in the proband sentences, so father's transcript left not reported. Tenosynovitis marked observed from ultrasound 'synovial hyperplasia surrounding extensor tendons' (word tenosynovitis not used for her). Fever checklist left not reported: the paper excludes only 'prolong fever or fever without source'. Not recorded as features: 'Levels of complements C3, C4 ... were all negative' (ambiguous for complement levels) and HLA-B27 genotype negative (genotype, not phenotype). Chest radiograph negative recorded as written, not as interstitial lung disease. Father's 'lacks clinical BS/EOS phenotype' recorded as one excluded feature; no checklist items excluded from it. No contradictions found.

study_type.span: Here we describes a case of BS/EOS with a novel C483W mutation in the NOD2 gene.

treatment_summary.value: emollients and topical steroid for skin lesions (limited effect); oral methotrexate 10 mg/m^2/week (arthritis progressed); oral prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day (rashes mitigated, arthritis not satisfactorily controlled); adalimumab from 5 months after initial treatment (noticeable improvement)
span: Emollients and topical steroid were prescribed for the control of her skin lesions with limited effect.
Oral methotrexate at a dose of 10 mg/m^2/week was prescribed for the control of her arthritis but the swelling and inflammation continues to progress.
Additional treatment with 1 mg/kg/day of oral prednisolone greatly mitigated the rashes, but its effect on arthritis control was not satisfying.
Adalimumab, a monoclonal antibody against TNF-α, was prescribed 5 months following her initial treatment with noticeable improvement.

functional_evidence_statement.value: HEK293T NOD2 overexpression NF-κB luciferase test: C483W confirmed gain-of-function; p-NFκB+ cells 20.5% of CD11b+ cells in the proband (father 10.9%, mother 0.9%, healthy controls 5.1%, R334W BS control 28.1%); plasma IL-6 and TNF-α elevated in the proband
span: The results supported that the C483W mutation was confirmed to be a gain-of-function mutation.
The p-NFκB^+/CD11b^+ cells account for 20.5%, 10.9%, 0.9%, 5.1% and 28.1% of all CD11b^+ cells in the proband, her father, mother, healthy controls and the BS/EOS control, respectively.
NFκB autoactivation was observed in CD11b^+ cells harboring NOD2 C483W and R334W mutant
the level of plasma cytokines IL-6 and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) were also elevated in the proband and the BS/EOS (R334W) control
